components.what_it_is: The estate's runtime-identity + secret substrate: SPIRE (server+agent+spire-controller-manager+spiffe-csi-driver+OIDC Discovery Provider) as the workload attestation CA, Istio (base+istiod) consuming SPIRE identity via the documented Workload API socket integration (not istio-csr), mesh-wide STRICT mTLS, OpenBao (dev-mode) with jwt auth against SPIRE's OIDC JWKS, and a ping/pong demo pair proving SPIFFE-principal-based AuthorizationPolicy.
components.how_it_runs: Flux-reconciled: HelmReleases (spire-crds, spire, istio-base, istiod, openbao) applied by up.sh and reconciled via `flux reconcile helmrelease` (timeout-bounded). ClusterSPIFFEID, PeerAuthentication, AuthorizationPolicy, Job (openbao-jwt-setup), and the ping/pong Deployments are plain kubectl-applied manifests, not part of a Kustomization/ResourceSet tree for this ticket (14) — no distribution/ layer wraps identity itself.
components.evidence_of_working: verify-identity.sh: offline PyYAML-based structural asserts (SPIRE controller-manager/OIDC/CSI enabled, trust domain acme.internal, agent socket path, istiod caName absent + ENABLE_CA_SERVER not false, meshConfig trustDomain, spire sidecar-injection template mounts csi.spiffe.io, PeerAuthentication STRICT, ClusterSPIFFEID className set + scheme-less authz principals) plus a bounded LIVE tail (kubectl --context kind-driftwood) that checks SPIRE/istiod/OpenBao pods, webhook caBundle populated, ping's istio-proxy sidecar Ready and holds a spiffe://acme.internal SVID, and ping→pong returns HTTP 200 over mTLS. Comments document three live-discovered bugs (ticket 04: ENABLE_CA_SERVER false broke the webhook; ticket 04/11: double-prefixed spiffe:// principal; ticket 11: className omission left ClusterSPIFFEID silently unreconciled) each now fixed and asserted against regression.

components.what_it_is: Kyverno→SPIRE posture projection (ticket 15): a MutatingPolicy (stamp-posture) that stamps posture.acme.io/version from the validated policy-as-versioned.dev/policy-version claim (the only writer, unconditional overwrite), a ValidatingPolicy (posture-trust-boundary) that Denies any posture label not equal to its claim, and a second ClusterSPIFFEID that bakes posture/<vN> as a leading SVID path segment, partitioned (via a DoesNotExist/Exists matchExpression pair) against identity's base mesh ClusterSPIFFEID so a pod never matches both.
components.how_it_runs: NOT Flux-reconciled directly. up.sh is explicitly labelled 'DEMO PATH, not delivery' — it calls distribution/render-and-prove.py to render each declared version from the real committed distribution/policies/v<version>/ tree, proves the result with `kubectl kustomize` (an independent builder), then kubectl-applies only the rendered VERSIONED copies (stamp-posture-<v>, posture-trust-boundary-<v>) plus the unversioned posture ClusterSPIFFEID (not part of the versioned/renderer tree) straight onto the existing driftwood KinD cluster. tests/ (kyverno-test.yaml matrices) are dev/CI tooling, deliberately excluded from the kustomization.yaml resources list.
components.evidence_of_working: verify-posture-projection.sh: offline `kyverno test` runs against tests/stamp-posture and tests/posture-trust-boundary (mutate-stamps-and-clobbers-forgery matrix; deny-forged/mismatched-posture matrix, with skip cases for out-of-scope pods) plus a PyYAML structural check (posture segment leads /ns/ in the SPIFFE template, className set, base/posture ClusterSPIFFEIDs share className and are a strict selector partition) and a bounded LIVE tail that server-dry-run applies a forged pod (must be denied) and a clobber pod (posture must reset to the real claim). Comments record a live-discovered bug (ticket 11: missing className left the CRD silently unreconciled with .status.stats permanently empty, and an overlapping selector caused nondeterministic SVID flips between base/posture identity across pod restarts) — both fixed and asserted against regression.

components.what_it_is: Ticket 16: a controller (currency.py, pure Python stdlib, no pip deps) that re-evaluates posture *after* admission — closing the Kyverno-only-fires-at-admission gap. Reads the supported-version set (the same array the orphan-guard ranges) and, for any postured pod whose posture is no longer supported, either de-postures it (removes BOTH the posture label and the policy-version claim in one merge patch, so stamp-posture can't re-add it and posture-trust-boundary doesn't deny the update) or evicts it.
components.how_it_runs: Kubernetes CronJob (`* * * * *`, every minute, concurrencyPolicy Forbid, activeDeadlineSeconds 120) running `python3 /src/currency.py reconcile` in a bare python:3.12-slim image; currency.py is mounted from a ConfigMap (currency-controller-src) created by up.sh with --from-file, so there is one source of the code. RBAC (manifests/rbac.yaml) grants a dedicated ServiceAccount get/list/patch/delete on pods and get on resourcesets — the only grant in the estate that can patch/delete another workload's pod. In-cluster it talks to the API server via urllib + the mounted ServiceAccount token (no kubectl binary, no client libs).
components.evidence_of_working: verify-currency.sh: `currency.py selfcheck` (pure asserts: select_stale logic, retire/re-add currency transitions, deposture_patch removes exactly both labels), an offline `plan` invocation against a JSON fixture proving only the retired-version pod is selected, a cross-check against the live posture-policy source files (parses stamp-posture.yaml/posture-trust-boundary.yaml/clusterspiffeid-posture.yaml and asserts the removed labels take the pod out of scope for each), kubectl client-side dry-run of the manifests, and a bounded LIVE tail that (if the CronJob and any stale postured pod exist) triggers one manual Job run via `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/...` — this is a trigger-and-inspect check, not an assertion of the reconcile's actual effect.
